values.description: a zone adjacent to a continent (or around an island) that extends from the low water line to a depth at which there is usually a marked increase of slope towards oceanic depths

values.name: banks
values.description: elevations, typically located on a shelf, over which the depth of water is relatively shallow but sufficient for safe surface navigation

values.name: canyons
values.description: relatively narrow, deep depressions with steep sides, the bottom of which generally has a continuous slope

values.name: deep
values.description: a localized deep area within the confines of a larger feature, such as a trough, basin or trench

values.name: knolls
values.description: elevations rising generally more than 500 meters and less than 1,000 meters and of limited extent across the summits

values.name: saddle
values.description: a low part, resembling in shape a saddle, in a ridge or between contiguous seamounts

values.name: province
values.description: a region identifiable by a group of similar physiographic features whose characteristics are markedly in contrast with surrounding areas

values.name: valleys
values.description: a relatively shallow, wide depression, the bottom of which usually has a continuous gradient

values.name: apron
values.description: a gentle slope, with a generally smooth surface, particularly found around groups of islands and seamounts

values.name: furrow
values.description: a closed, linear, narrow, shallow depression

values.name: peak
values.description: a prominent elevation, part of a larger feature, either pointed or of very limited extent across the summit

values.name: tongue
values.description: an elongate (tongue-like) extension of a flat sea floor into an adjacent higher feature

values.name: ridges
values.description: long narrow elevations with steep sides

values.name: seachannels
values.description: continuously sloping, elongated depressions commonly found in fans or plains and customarily bordered by levees on one or two sides

values.name: sill
values.description: the low part of a gap or saddle separating basins

values.name: tablemounts (or guyots)
values.description: seamounts having a comparatively smooth, flat top

values.name: shelf valley
values.description: a valley on the shelf, generally the shoreward extension of a canyon

values.name: cordillera
values.description: an entire mountain system including the subordinate ranges, interior plateaus, and basins

values.name: shelf edge
values.description: a line along which there is a marked increase of slope at the outer margin of a continental shelf or island shelf

values.name: borderland
values.description: a region adjacent to a continent, normally occupied by or bordering a shelf, that is highly irregular with depths well in excess of those typical of a shelf

values.name: arrugado
values.description: an area of subdued corrugations off Baja California

values.name: levee
values.description: an embankment bordering a canyon, valley, or seachannel

values.name: pinnacle
values.description: a high tower or spire-shaped pillar of rock or coral, alone or cresting a summit

values.name: arch
values.description: a low bulge around the southeastern end of the island of Hawaii

values.name: continental rise
values.description: a gentle slope rising from oceanic depths towards the foot of a continental slope

values.name: mesa
values.description: an isolated, extensive, flat-topped elevation on the shelf, with relatively steep sides

values.name: moat
values.description: an annular depression that may not be continuous, located at the base of many seamounts, islands, and other isolated elevations

values.name: mountain
values.description: a well-delineated subdivision of a large and complex positive feature

values.name: peaks
values.description: prominent elevations, part of a larger feature, either pointed or of very limited extent across the summit

values.name: forest(s)
values.description: an area dominated by tree vegetation

values.name: cultivated area
values.description: an area under cultivation

values.name: grove
values.description: a small wooded area or collection of trees growing closely together, occurring naturally or deliberately planted

values.name: meadow
values.description: a small, poorly drained area dominated by grassy vegetation

values.name: vineyard
values.description: a planting of grapevines

values.name: scrubland
values.description: an area of low trees, bushes, and shrubs stunted by some environmental limitation

values.name: orchard(s)
values.description: a planting of fruit or nut trees

values.name: heath
values.description: an upland moor or sandy area dominated by low shrubby vegetation including heather

values.name: grassland
values.description: an area dominated by grass vegetation

values.name: tree(s)
values.description: a conspicuous tree used as a landmark

values.name: coconut grove
values.description: a planting of coconut trees

values.name: palm grove
values.description: a planting of palm trees

values.name: vineyards
values.description: plantings of grapevines

values.name: bush(es)
values.description: a small clump of conspicuous bushes in an otherwise bare area

values.name: fossilized forest
values.description: a forest fossilized by geologic processes and now exposed at the earth's surface

values.name: pine grove
values.description: a planting of pine trees

values.name: tundra
values.description: a marshy, treeless, high latitude plain, dominated by mosses, lichens, and low shrub vegetation under permafrost conditions

values.name: olive grove
values.description: a planting of olive trees
